class.name: WorldStreamer
class.brief_description: Streams the chunks of a large world in and out around a focus point.
class.description: WorldStreamer keeps only the part of a big world that is near the player in memory. The world is divided into a grid of cells of [member cell_size]. For every cell within [member load_radius] of the [member focus] the streamer looks up a scene file (using [member chunk_path_template] or a callback set with [method set_chunk_provider]), loads it on a background thread, and adds it as a child. Cells that are farther than [member unload_radius] are removed again. Loading uses [ResourceLoader] threaded requests and at most [member max_instantiations_per_frame] chunks are instantiated per frame, so walking through the world does not stall the game. A chunk scene is a normal scene: put the terrain, buildings, props and enemies of one cell in it, with the origin of the scene at the corner of the cell. The streamer moves the chunk root to the corner of its cell. [codeblock] var streamer = WorldStreamer.new() streamer.focus = ^"../Player" streamer.cell_size = 128.0 streamer.load_radius = 400.0 streamer.unload_radius = 500.0 streamer.chunk_path_template = "res://world/chunk_{x}_{z}.tscn" add_child(streamer) [/codeblock] Cells without a scene file are skipped silently, so the world may have holes (oceans, unfinished areas). Unload radius larger than the load radius gives hysteresis: a player pacing along a cell border does not make chunks flicker in and out. To reduce initial streaming spikes for cosmetic world chunks, call [method begin_loading_range_ramp] before the initial scene load. This starts with a smaller fraction of the configured 2D loading area (or 3D volume), then grows the active load radius to its full value in game time. Only new chunk requests are gated: the configured unload radius, loaded scenes, cell geometry and auxiliary source are unaffected. This may temporarily show less distant world detail, so use it only where gameplay/collision is independently ready. To reduce visible pop-in when the player runs or rides, optionally set [member velocity_hint] and [member lookahead_seconds]. The streamer orders already-eligible cells toward a bounded predicted position, but the actual focus and load/unload radii still determine residency. No extra cells are loaded, and [member max_instantiations_per_frame] still limits main-thread work. Optional local route hints can improve scenery arrival along a personal waypoint path. [method set_route_cells] accepts a bounded four-connected corridor from gameplay pathfinding; it changes scheduling priority inside the same focus radius, without allocating any additional world cells. This is distinct from the bounded auxiliary streaming source, which can include a few cells near a valid nearby waypoint. [b]Large worlds:[/b] when the chunks live under a [Node3D] set as [member chunk_parent] that is moved by [FloatingOrigin3D], the focus position is measured in that node's local space, so the grid stays in absolute world coordinates while the origin shifts.

method.name: advance_loading_range_ramp
method.description: Advances the opt-in loading area ramp using finite, positive game-time seconds. Called automatically once each engine internal process frame; manual calls are useful for deterministic simulations or tests. The full configured radius is reached after the optional delay and ramp duration.

method.name: begin_loading_range_ramp
method.description: Starts an opt-in startup loading area ramp without changing [member load_radius] or [member unload_radius]. Fractions are clamped to 0.05–1; delay to 0–60 seconds and duration to 0–120 seconds. For a 2D grid, 0.25 loads half the configured distance; for a 3D grid the distance is the cube root of the requested volume fraction. The initial player cell remains eligible. A zero delay and duration restores full range immediately. Runtime scene creation still uses the usual per-frame budgets; auxiliary source radius is not scaled.

method.name: cancel_loading_range_ramp
method.description: Immediately restores the configured full loading radius and schedules a regular streaming queue refresh, without synchronously loading additional chunks.

method.name: advance_chunk_pressure
method.description: Pure bounded slow-frame pressure step. A frame longer than 30 ms adds 0.16, a frame shorter than 20 ms subtracts 0.05, and intermediate frames hold pressure. Invalid elapsed time is ignored, and pressure stays within 0 to 1.

method.name: calculate_adaptive_instantiation_slots
method.description: Returns the adaptive number of chunk integration slots for a configured limit, reducing by one for pressure at least 0.4 and by two for pressure at least 0.8, with a minimum of one.

method.name: calculate_adaptive_chunk_work_usec
method.description: Returns the adaptive soft CPU-time limit in microseconds; high pressure scales the configured value to 75% or 50%, but never raises the configured cap. Zero disables the time cap.

method.name: calculate_adaptive_unload_slots
method.description: Returns an unload count (0–64): a positive configured limit falls to 75% at pressure 0.4 and 50% at pressure 0.8 (rounded up, minimum one). Zero remains unlimited; non-finite pressure is treated as zero.

method.name: get_effective_load_radius
method.description: Actual player-centered load radius used by the current streaming scheduler and focus readiness snapshots. During a ramp, this is [member load_radius] multiplied by the square root of the loaded area fraction for XY/XZ, or the cube root for XYZ. When the ramp is disabled or finished it equals [member load_radius].

method.name: get_loading_range_area_percent
method.description: Current requested main-focus loading area or volume, expressed as 5–100 percent during a ramp and 100 percent otherwise. Read-only, with no chunk creation.

method.name: is_loading_range_ramping
method.description: Whether the startup loading-range delay or expansion is still pending. Defaults to false and becomes false when full range is restored or canceled.

method.name: get_effective_unloads_per_update
method.description: Current limit for far-away chunk teardown. Zero means unlimited legacy cleanup. Adaptive streaming reduces positive limits on slow frames and restores throughput on recovery; manual unload_all bypasses this budget.

method.name: get_effective_instantiations_per_frame
method.description: Returns the current adaptive or legacy limit for procedural generation and threaded scene activation.

method.name: get_effective_chunk_work_usec
method.description: Returns the current soft deadline in microseconds. Individual chunks are indivisible.

method.name: get_streaming_frame_pressure_percent
method.description: Returns 0 to 100 for the measured render-frame backpressure. Only updated on the streamer's internal process when adaptivity is enabled.

method.name: should_defer_predicted_chunk_work
method.description: Pure admission helper: returns true only when a second or later scene work unit would exceed a positive shared CPU budget based on prior measured time plus the forecast. Unknown estimates, disabled budgets and first attempts always return false.

method.name: update_chunk_work_estimate
method.description: Pure bounded quarter-rate exponential moving average for measured per-chunk main-thread CPU microseconds. Returns the previous estimate for a zero/negative sample and clamps positive estimates to 1000000. The engine records separate procedural and threaded-finalization forecasts.

method.name: get_estimated_generator_work_usec
method.description: Observed moving-average main-thread microseconds for procedural generation and node adoption, clamped to 1000000. No prediction until at least one positive sample. Resets when the generator or streaming grid changes.

method.name: get_estimated_finalization_work_usec
method.description: Observed moving-average microseconds for ready-threaded-scene finalization, excluding background resource decoding. Reset on provider/template/grid changes.

method.name: get_last_predicted_deferred_chunk_count
method.description: Number of already-wanted procedural or ready-threaded cells deferred in the last frame by the optional cost forecast (not by the regular count or wall-clock limit). Recomputed on every internal update or explicit refresh.

method.name: get_last_frame_chunk_work_usec
method.description: Returns the elapsed main-thread microseconds of the last stream integration frame, covering both procedural generator+adoption and threaded scene finalization. Resource decoding on worker threads is not included.

method.name: get_last_frame_chunk_attempt_count
method.description: Returns the number of generator calls and loaded-scene finalization attempts in the last stream integration frame, including empty and failed chunks.

method.name: cell_to_world
method.description: Returns the corner with the lowest coordinates of [param cell], in the local space of the chunk parent.

method.name: clear_cached_chunks
method.description: Frees all detached, explicitly cached procedural scene roots, and resets cache hit/eviction diagnostics. Does not unload resident chunks or change the configured [member max_cached_chunks] cap.

method.name: clear_auxiliary_source
method.description: Disables the optional secondary streaming source. Chunks no longer wanted by the primary focus or the auxiliary source are released on the next update according to the primary unload radius. Repeated calls are harmless. Does not immediately destroy unrelated primary chunks.

method.name: clear_route_cells
method.description: Clears the optional route-cell priority hint. Ordinary movement and camera priority remain active. Does not immediately unload any chunk or alter the player-centered streaming radius.

method.name: get_auxiliary_source_position
method.description: Returns the last secondary streaming source position in the chunk parent's coordinate space. It does not imply the source is active; check [method has_auxiliary_source].

method.name: get_auxiliary_source_radius
method.description: Returns the active auxiliary source's effective radius, capped to twice [member cell_size]. Returns [code]0.0[/code] when disabled.

method.name: get_auxiliary_source_failed_count
method.description: Number of failed cells currently intersecting the nearby auxiliary source. Failure prevents readiness, even when a source has no remaining queued work.

method.name: get_auxiliary_source_pending_count
method.description: Count of source cells that are neither settled nor failed. When [param require_visual_details] is true, loaded chunks with pending staged visuals also count as pending. Queries return zero for disabled or remote sources.

method.name: get_focus_streaming_status
method.description: Read-only World Partition-style completion snapshot for the main observer's current [member load_radius]. Returns [code]total[/code], [code]completed[/code], [code]pending[/code], [code]failed[/code], [code]progress[/code] (fraction 0–1), [code]ready[/code] and [code]truncated[/code]. Loaded chunks and intentionally absent cells count as complete; failed cells do not. With [param require_visual_details] enabled, a generated chunk remains pending until [method mark_visual_details_ready] is called. The count uses the same bounded main streaming grid (maximum 16,384 cells), excluding the auxiliary waypoint source. A disabled streamer or invalid input yields no eligible cells and [code]ready = false[/code]. Truncated grids never report ready or full progress. This method never starts generation, requests resources, activates physics, or changes world state. For a separate waypoint, use [method get_auxiliary_source_progress].

method.name: get_auxiliary_source_progress
method.description: Read-only 0–1 completion fraction for the active nearby secondary source, across at most 64 grid cells. Loaded scenes and intentionally empty (missing) cells count as settled. Failures never count as complete. If [param require_visual_details] is true, also waits for [method mark_visual_details_ready] on staged chunks. Returns zero when disabled, dormant, or no eligible cells are found. This does not request loads, allocate new chunks, change scheduling, or guarantee navigation/physics readiness.

method.name: get_chunk
method.description: Returns the loaded chunk of [param cell], or [code]null[/code] if that cell is not loaded.

method.name: advance_cached_chunk_retention
method.description: Advances the TTL clock for detached procedural roots once per internal process frame. Opt-in count and soft CPU-time budgets may defer expired roots across successive frames. Headless tests can advance with positive game-time deltas. Invalid deltas are ignored and a step is bounded to 120 seconds; resident world cells are never affected.

method.name: get_cached_chunk_bytes
method.description: Total game-reported estimated bytes retained in detached cached procedural chunks, excluding shared assets, pending frees and runtime GPU allocation. Count-only legacy entries contribute zero. Not actual measured RAM/VRAM.

method.name: get_cached_chunk_count
method.description: Number of detached, cached procedural scene roots. These do not count toward [method get_loaded_count] and cannot be returned by [method get_chunk].

method.name: get_chunk_cache_hit_count
method.description: Count of cached scene roots successfully reattached instead of recreated by the procedural generator. A cache hit still uses a normal main-thread integration slot.

method.name: get_last_cached_expiration_count
method.description: Number of expired detached scene roots retired by the latest cleanup pass. Zero after manual cache clear or an idle/empty step.

method.name: get_last_cached_expiration_work_usec
method.description: Main-thread microseconds spent scanning and retiring expired cache entries during the latest pass. One individual destructor can exceed the soft CPU-time cap.

method.name: get_last_deferred_cached_expiration_count
method.description: Already-expired cached roots deferred by the latest count or CPU-time budget, drained on subsequent frames. With both limits zero, the legacy cleanup completes in one pass.

method.name: get_chunk_cache_expiration_count
method.description: Number of detached procedural scenes retired due to the optional age limit, separate from capacity-based cache evictions. Reset by [method clear_cached_chunks].

method.name: get_chunk_cache_eviction_count
method.description: Count of oldest cached roots removed because the configured cap was exceeded. Does not include explicit cache clearing.

method.name: get_chunk_generator
method.description: Returns the callback set with [method set_chunk_generator].

method.name: get_chunk_provider
method.description: Returns the callback set with [method set_chunk_provider].

method.name: get_loaded_cells
method.description: Returns the cells whose chunks are currently loaded.

method.name: get_last_unload_work_usec
method.description: Microseconds spent selecting and deactivating expired chunk roots during the last refresh, including their synchronous unload callbacks. Zero when no expired cells exist or after [method unload_all]. Deferred scene memory reclamation is not included. Compare with [member max_unload_work_usec] when profiling spikes.

method.name: get_last_unload_count
method.description: Number of distant cells actually unloaded during the last streaming refresh. Zero when none were eligible or immediately after [method unload_all]. This count is independent of scene creation and native simulation LOD transitions.

method.name: get_last_deferred_unload_count
method.description: Number of out-of-range resident cells whose unload was deferred by the last refresh's [member max_unloads_per_update] budget. Each refresh recomputes eligibility from the current focus, so returning toward the old location cancels stale cleanup. This snapshot may become outdated before the next refresh.

method.name: get_loaded_count
method.description: Returns the number of loaded chunks.

method.name: get_pending_count
method.description: Returns the number of chunks that are being loaded in the background.

method.name: get_pending_visual_details_count
method.description: Counts resident chunks which have reported unfinished optional cosmetic detail work, independently of queued procedural cells and threaded scene loads. A chunk can be fully playable while its grass, flowers or small debris are still being generated within a graphics frame budget. Only chunks implementing [code]has_pending_visual_detail()[/code] returning [code]true[/code] at adoption are counted. The counter is automatically cleared when such chunks are unloaded, even if their visual tasks never finish.

method.name: get_queued_generation_count
method.description: Returns the number of procedural cells waiting for the chunk generator callback. Unlike [method get_pending_count], which counts scene files loaded in background threads, this measures the main-thread generation backlog. Pending procedural cells are rebuilt from the current load area on each streaming update, so teleportation and rapid turns cannot accumulate an obsolete backlog. The value can be included in a game benchmark to diagnose world-streaming pop-in or CPU hitches. No additional assets or chunks are allocated by this query.

method.name: get_route_cells
method.description: Returns a copy of the current optional route-cell priority hint. It does not imply that every route cell is currently loaded: only cells already inside the primary streaming radius are eligible for route priority.

method.name: has_auxiliary_source
method.description: Returns whether a secondary source is configured. A source whose position is more than [member load_radius] plus one cell width from the primary focus is considered dormant and does not allocate or retain remote scene chunks.

method.name: is_cell_loaded
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the chunk of [param cell] is loaded.

method.name: mark_visual_details_ready
method.description: Marks optional staged cosmetic work complete for a previously loaded chunk. Does nothing for unknown or already-completed cells. Emits [signal chunk_visual_details_ready] once, without affecting gameplay state, chunk residency, load/unload radius or the procedural generation budget. Call this after cosmetic MultiMesh categories are finished.

method.name: refresh
method.description: Updates the streaming immediately instead of waiting for [member update_interval]. If [param retry] is [code]true[/code], cells that had no scene or failed to load are tried again, for example after new chunk files were added.

method.name: set_auxiliary_source
method.description: Cgame extension: registers one extra bounded streaming source for nearby waypoints, portal previews and cinematic targets, inspired by Unreal Engine World Partition streaming sources. Its requested [param radius] is capped at two cell widths, and its [param position] only contributes cells once within [member load_radius] plus one cell width of the active focus. Distant pins never create an independent loaded world. Auxiliary cells are interleaved with primary cells and share the existing main-thread, async loading, and per-frame instantiation budgets. The primary focus cell is always first; the source never affects authoritative game state or network replication. Inputs must be finite, and [param radius] positive. After calling this method, the queue is updated in the following internal process step; call [method refresh] if immediate synchronous scheduling is required.

method.name: set_chunk_generator
method.description: Sets a callback that builds the chunk of a cell in code, for worlds generated from a seed instead of stored as scene files. It receives the cell as a [Vector3i] and returns the chunk as a [Node], or [code]null[/code] for an empty cell. It runs on the main thread, at most [member max_instantiations_per_frame] times per frame, nearest cells first, and the focus may have moved away by the time a queued cell would be built, in which case it is skipped. When a generator is set, [member chunk_path_template] and [method set_chunk_provider] are ignored.

method.name: set_chunk_provider
method.description: Sets a callback used instead of [member chunk_path_template] to find the scene of a cell. It receives the cell as a [Vector3i] and returns the scene path as a [String], or an empty string if the cell has no chunk. This allows chunk lookup from a database or a procedural generator.

method.name: set_route_cells
method.description: Supplies a game-planned corridor of up to 64 orthogonally adjacent streaming cell coordinates in traversal order. Returns [code]false[/code] without altering the previous hint when too many cells, diagonal jumps, duplicates, or invalid plane coordinates are supplied. When the first coordinate matches the player's current cell, the native streamer promotes the next eligible route cells while interleaving regular nearby chunks to prevent starvation. The route NEVER extends load/unload radii, skips CPU/instantiation budgets, creates remote scenery or changes authoritative gameplay. Use [AStarGrid2D] or another game path planner to avoid blocked cells before submitting this hint. Updating a matching route is idempotent. When the streaming axes or cell size changes, this hint is cleared automatically.

method.name: unload_all
method.description: Frees every loaded chunk and all detached cache entries immediately, even when [member max_unloads_per_update] is set. They are loaded again at the next update while the focus is nearby.

method.name: world_to_cell
method.description: Returns the cell that contains [param position] on the streamed [member axes].

method.name: get_tick_throttled_count
method.description: Returns the number of loaded chunk roots actually receiving a positive cosmetic tick interval. Roots without [code]set_streaming_tick_interval(seconds)[/code] are not counted. Does not alter CPU update frequency on its own.

method.name: get_simulation_active_count
method.description: Number of resident chunks currently assigned to the active simulation tier. The scene root must opt in to actually change its cosmetic processing.

method.name: is_auxiliary_source_ready
method.description: Whether all cells intersecting the currently active, nearby auxiliary source are settled and no cells have failed. Intentionally empty cells count as settled. With [param require_visual_details] true, waits for optional staged cosmetic completion. This is a visual streaming readiness snapshot, not a safe-teleport, physics, or server-authority barrier. Disabled or remote sources return false.

method.name: is_cell_tick_throttled
method.description: Whether the given loaded chunk root currently receives a positive, reduced-frequency cosmetic tick interval. Returns false for unloaded cells and roots without the callback.

method.name: is_cell_simulation_active
method.description: Returns whether the loaded chunk has an active simulation tier. Unloaded cells always return false.

members.member: Opt-in slow-frame streaming backpressure. When enabled, high render-frame latency temporarily reduces per-frame chunk count and the microsecond budget, while never dropping below one integration slot. Normal frame times gradually recover configured limits. No change is made to load radius, unload radius, queued cells, authoritative world simulation, or asynchronous resource loading. Disabled by default for compatibility.

Which axes make up the grid. [constant AXES_XZ] streams on the ground plane of a 3D world, [constant AXES_XY] is for 2D worlds, and [constant AXES_XYZ] also streams along the vertical axis. Changing it unloads every chunk.

Edge length of a cell. Pick a size so that one chunk holds a reasonable amount of content: big enough that loading is not constant, small enough that a chunk loads quickly. Changing it unloads every chunk.
Node that the chunks are added to. By default they are children of the streamer. Set it to a [Node3D] or [Node2D] to control their transform, for example to move them with [FloatingOrigin3D].

Path of a chunk scene with [code]{x}[/code], [code]{y}[/code] and [code]{z}[/code] replaced by the cell coordinates, for example [code]res://world/chunk_{x}_{z}.tscn[/code]. Ignored when a provider was set with [method set_chunk_provider].
If [code]false[/code], no chunks are loaded or unloaded. Chunks that are already loaded stay.

Opt-in threshold for quickly refreshing the chunk priority queue after a large camera turn. When [member view_direction] changes this many degrees from the direction used by the last queue rebuild, and [member view_priority] is positive, the engine may refresh scheduling earlier than [member update_interval], but no more frequently than every 50 milliseconds. A value of [code]0[/code] disables the fast path and preserves legacy update timing. The threshold is clamped from 0 through 180 degrees. It changes scheduling only: load/unload radii, CPU work budgets and scene ownership stay unchanged.
Node whose position decides which chunks are needed, usually the player or the camera. It can be a [Node3D] or a [Node2D]. If it is empty or invalid, [member focus_position] is used.
Position used when no [member focus] node is set. Update it from a script for custom streaming points.

How many seconds ahead movement-based streaming should prioritize chunk requests. The value is clamped to [code]0.0[/code] through [code]4.0[/code]. Default [code]0.0[/code] keeps legacy distance-only streaming. Prediction is further limited to one cell width and 40% of [member load_radius]. It never enlarges the set of loaded cells.
Cells closer than this distance (measured to the cell's box) to the focus are loaded.
Maximum number of chunks loading in the background at the same time.

Optional maximum retention time for detached, immutable procedural scene roots, clamped to 0–120 game-time seconds. Zero disables expiry for legacy projects. A positive limit releases cached roots when old, even while the player stands still and the count/estimated-byte budgets are not full. This does not unload active world cells, server/physics/quest entities or additional streaming sources. A cache hit before expiry retains normal scene adoption and work budgets; an expired cell is regenerated on the next request. The engine automatically advances time while running; [method advance_cached_chunk_retention] can drive deterministic headless tests. Use [method get_chunk_cache_expiration_count] to monitor expired roots separately from capacity evictions.

Optional per-frame cap (0–16) on destruction of expired detached procedural chunk roots, with zero preserving the legacy unlimited TTL pass. The engine always retires at least one overdue root, then defers the remaining roots to later internal frames. Explicit TTL changes and manual cache clearing remain synchronous.

Optional per-frame soft CPU-time budget (0–1000000 microseconds) for TTL expiry. Zero disables the time limit. Once the first overdue root is retired, no further destructor is started if the budget elapsed. Individual scene deletion can exceed its budget; both this and [member max_cached_expirations_per_frame] apply together. See [method get_last_cached_expiration_work_usec] and [method get_last_deferred_cached_expiration_count].

Optional estimated memory budget for detached procedural scene roots, clamped to 0–268435456 bytes (256 MiB). Zero preserves original count-only caching. A positive value requires each opted-in chunk to implement [code]get_streaming_cache_cost_bytes() -> int[/code] and return a positive estimate no greater than the cap. Unknown, invalid and oversized values decline caching; overbudget caches evict oldest unrequested roots first. These gameplay estimates do not guarantee physical RAM/VRAM, include shared assets or track pending queued frees. Decreasing the budget immediately trims detached roots and never touches active/authoritative world residency.

Opt-in bounded cache for unloaded, procedural Node roots that implement [code]can_cache_streaming_chunk() -> bool[/code] and explicitly return [code]true[/code]. Zero preserves normal unload-and-free behavior; values are clamped to 0–16 complete scene roots. Cached roots are detached and do not render or simulate, but still retain memory. Least-recent entries are evicted first, but cells requested again by the current focus/source take precedence over nonrequested cached cells. Returning to the exact cell reattaches through the ordinary budgeted load path and optionally invokes [code]on_streaming_cache_restored()[/code] after adoption. Cached roots are cleared on grid/parent/generator changes, manual unload and destruction; only immutable client visuals should opt in. Not for authoritative entities, physics, quest state, or network-owned objects.

Optional cost-forecast admission for procedural and threaded-ready cell activation, using independent 1/4 exponential moving averages of observed main-thread microseconds. Enabled only when [member max_chunk_work_usec] is positive. After at least one completed cell work unit in this frame, a candidate is postponed when its predicted cost plus already-measured work exceeds the shared frame budget. The first cell is never blocked, unknown costs do not block, and a single noninterruptible scene activation can exceed the soft limit. All normal loading priorities and cell count budgets still apply. Zero CPU time budget or default disabled mode retain legacy behavior. The budget uses real measurements, not GPU time or background texture decoding; estimates reset when the corresponding generator/provider/grid changes.

Soft CPU-time budget, in microseconds, shared across finished-scene activation and procedural chunk generation during one streaming update. Both paths use the same frame start timestamp. Once at least one chunk has been processed, no more chunks are integrated after the budget expires. A single chunk cannot be interrupted and may take longer than the budget. Enable [member adaptive_chunk_budget_enabled] to temporarily reduce effective limits during sustained slow frames; call [method get_effective_chunk_work_usec] for the resulting cap. The value is clamped to [code]0[/code] through [code]1000000[/code]; [code]0[/code] disables time slicing while keeping [member max_instantiations_per_frame] active. Also works with [method refresh].

Optional soft CPU-time budget in microseconds for deactivating obsolete chunk scene roots, measured from unload selection through synchronous node removal and signals. Requires [member max_unloads_per_update] greater than zero; zero preserves count-only unloading and the original unlimited legacy path. At least one eligible chunk can be retired even if its work exceeds the cap, so this cannot provide a hard real-time guarantee. The value is clamped to 0–1000000. The count limit always applies too; [method unload_all], scene-tree teardown and grid resets bypass the time cap. Queued scene memory freeing may happen later and is not included.

Optional maximum number of far-away chunk roots unloaded per streaming refresh. Zero preserves the original unlimited teardown behavior; positive values are clamped to 1–64. On teleport or a rapidly moving observer, the streamer unloads farthest expired cells first (stable coordinate ties) and leaves other expired cells resident temporarily, re-evaluating them on the next refresh. Nearby auxiliary streaming sources still protect their cells. With [member adaptive_chunk_budget_enabled], positive limits decrease during slow frames without stopping cleanup; see [method get_effective_unloads_per_update]. Does not limit [method unload_all], scene-tree teardown, or grid configuration resets. Only enable for chunk scene roots whose gameplay/physics state is safe to retain temporarily; delayed cleanup increases peak memory residency.

Maximum number of chunks activated during one native streaming update, counting both finished background scene loads and procedural generator calls against the same budget. Once the limit is reached, remaining cells stay queued for a later update. A generator that returns [code]null[/code] or fails still consumes a slot, since the callback may already have done expensive CPU work. Combine with [member max_chunk_work_usec] to load several cheap chunks without scheduling more work after a costly chunk.

Caps state changes on already-loaded chunks to 1–64 per streaming update. Near-field reactivations are always considered before far-field deactivations. Newly instantiated chunks receive an initial tier within the existing chunk creation budget.
If [code]true[/code], the root of every chunk is moved to the corner of its cell. Turn it off if the chunk scenes are already authored at their world position.
Extra distance in metres an already-active chunk retains simulation after leaving [member simulation_radius]. Inactive chunks only reactivate when entering the inner radius. Clamped to 0–1000 metres.

Unreal-style optional cosmetic update-frequency tier for streamed chunks. Negative (default) disables and avoids the per-chunk scan; 0–100000 chooses the full-rate near radius. Chunk roots must implement [code]set_streaming_tick_interval(seconds: float)[/code]. Outside this radius plus [member tick_throttle_hysteresis], opted-in roots receive [member tick_throttle_interval]; when returning inside the radius they receive zero (full rate). Existing root transitions are bounded and nearest near-recoveries run first. Purely advisory: the root chooses which script effects to throttle, never physics or gameplay authority.

Positive seconds between expensive cosmetic scene updates in the distant tier. Clamped to 0–1 second; zero restores full-rate callbacks over the configured transition budget. The actual chunk script must accumulate delta and decide how to defer work; setting this does not affect engine physics ticks.

Extra distance required before promoting a near full-rate chunk to the reduced-frequency tier. Clamped 0–1000; returning within the normal radius restores near rate immediately, subject to the transition budget.

Maximum number of existing loaded chunk callback rate changes (1–64) during one streaming refresh. New chunk initial tick rates are set before scene attachment and are already covered by the normal chunk generation/activation budget.

Opt-in distance in metres for cosmetic/script simulation on resident chunks. Negative (default) preserves all legacy chunk processing and avoids per-chunk simulation scans. The streamer calls a chunk root's optional [code]set_streaming_simulation_active(active: bool)[/code] when its tier changes; it never alters scene descendants, terrain, physics or networking by itself. State changes do not load or unload cells. Clamped to -1 (disabled) or 0–100000 metres.
Loaded cells farther than this distance from the focus are freed. Values below [member load_radius] are treated as equal to it.

Optional camera-space horizontal half field of view for scheduling. The default 180 degrees preserves the existing heading-only priority. With positive [member view_priority] and a nonzero [member view_direction], values from 1 to 179.99 degrees smoothly reduce the view bonus near the cone edge and remove it outside the cone; they do not cull chunks, change cell residency, or consume extra requests. Use a conservative margin for the camera and treat orthographic or unknown cameras as 180 degrees. Invalid or non-finite settings are rejected or clamped to 1–180 degrees.

Optional normalized camera heading. When [member view_priority] is positive, both procedural chunk generation and completed threaded scene activation prefer nearby cells within the camera's view direction. A zero or non-finite direction disables view weighting, returning to movement-only priority. This is independent of residency and does not add extra cells to memory.

Weight from 0 to 1 for camera-visible chunk priority. Zero preserves movement-only streaming; positive values favor camera-facing cells without starving nearby cells behind the player. The weight is applied equally to queued generators and finished threaded scene loads.

Estimated velocity of the player or camera, in metres per second, used only to prioritize chunks within [member load_radius]. The ignored grid axis is discarded. Non-finite hints are rejected, while zero velocity preserves nearest-first loading. Update this when the character moves; reset it after a teleport or network correction.
Time in seconds between two evaluations of which cells to load and unload. Checking a few times per second is enough; [code]0[/code] checks every frame.

signal.name: chunk_tick_interval_changed
signal.description: Emitted when an already-loaded opted-in chunk changes its effective cosmetic update interval. Initial chunk setup is available through [method is_cell_tick_throttled] and [signal chunk_loaded].

signal.name: chunk_simulation_changed
signal.description: Emitted for a change of an already-loaded chunk's simulation tier. Initial tier selection is available through [method is_cell_simulation_active] after [signal chunk_loaded].

signal.name: chunk_load_failed
signal.description: Emitted when a chunk scene could not be loaded or instantiated. The cell is not retried until [method refresh] is called with [code]retry[/code].

signal.name: chunk_visual_details_ready
signal.description: Emitted once after a loaded chunk finishes optional staged cosmetic work. Core world objects are accessible from [signal chunk_loaded] before this signal. Unloading a chunk clears its pending visual status without emitting this completion signal.

signal.name: chunk_loaded
signal.description: Emitted after the chunk of [param cell] was added to the scene.

signal.name: chunk_unloaded
signal.description: Emitted when the chunk of [param cell] was removed, either because the focus moved away or because the chunk was freed elsewhere.

constants.constant: Grid on the ground plane of a 3D world; height is ignored.
Three dimensional grid; chunks are also streamed along the vertical axis.
